name: Shadow Credentials - pywhisker
description: Shadow Credentials abuse: with write access to a target's msDS-KeyCredentialLink, pywhisker adds a certificate/key you control, yielding a PFX you can use with PKINIT to authenticate as that target. Alternative path to Pass the Certificate.

examples.label: Add shadow credentials to a target user

notes:
pyWhisker adds a Key Credential (msDS-KeyCredentialLink) to an account you control via GenericWrite, giving you a cert to PKINIT as them (shadow credentials).
Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 19 (Password Attacks)

recommended.note: Request a TGT with the added key.

defense.why_it_works: pyWhisker abuses write access to a target's msDS-KeyCredentialLink (Shadow Credentials) to add an attacker key, then authenticates as that account via PKINIT.
defense.prerequisites: Write access (GenericWrite/KeyCredentialLink) over the target AD object.
defense.impact: Authentication as the target account via a forged key credential - account takeover without changing its password.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1649] modification of msDS-KeyCredentialLink (5136 on the attribute); subsequent PKINIT 4768 for that account.
defense.artifacts: A new KeyCredentialLink value; the generated cert/key; a PKINIT logon for the target.
defense.prevention: Audit/restrict write access to msDS-KeyCredentialLink; monitor 5136 on that attribute; enforce Key Trust hardening.
defense.evasion: Removing the added key credential after use hides the change; PKINIT then looks like normal certificate auth.
defense.misconfiguration: Pass-the-Certificate (PtC) attacks exploit ADCS certificate abuse (ESC1/ESC8) combined with Kerberos PKINIT. Shadow credentials (pywhisker) exploit write access to msDS-KeyCredentialLink to add a certificate-based authentication mechanism to any account. Pass-the-Ticket works because Kerberos tickets are extractable from LSASS memory.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# msDS-KeyCredentialLink writable by attacker (GenericWrite on target account):
# pywhisker.py -t targetuser -a add
# Adds a fake device credential -> obtain certificate for targetuser
# -> PKINIT TGT as targetuser -> NTLM hash via UnPAC

# LSASS memory contains TGTs for all logged-in users:
# Mimikatz: sekurlsa::tickets /export
# Rubeus: dump /all
defense.secure_config:
# Prevent msDS-KeyCredentialLink abuse:
# Audit who has GenericWrite on privileged accounts
# Only SYSTEM/DCs should write msDS-KeyCredentialLink
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity admin -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'Write'}

# Prevent ticket extraction:
# Enable Credential Guard (blocks LSASS memory reads)
# Protected Users group members: tickets not cached in LSASS

# ADCS: prevent ESC1/ESC8 (see those cards)
# Monitor: Event 4768 with certificate auth, Event 4769 unusual ticket lifetimes
